title: FEC operates without a quorum for nearly 80% of Trump's second term
description_short: FEC operates without a quorum for nearly 80% of Trump's second term
description_medium: Trump sent longtime Democratic FEC commissioner Ellen Weintraub a January 31, 2025 letter purporting to remove her; Weintraub disputed the legality of the action. After additional commissioner departures, the FEC fell below its four-member voting threshold on May 1, 2025. NOTUS reported in March 2026 that the agency had 195 pending enforcement matters and later calculated that it had lacked a quorum for nearly 80% of Trump's second term. The prolonged lack of quorum prevented substantive enforcement votes.
description_long: Trump sent Democratic FEC commissioner Ellen Weintraub a January 31, 2025 letter purporting to remove her from office. Weintraub disputed the action's legality. Additional commissioner departures later left the agency below its four-member voting threshold on May 1, following Allen Dickerson's April 30 departure. The loss of quorum prevented substantive enforcement votes, creating an institutional consequence separate from the dispute over Weintraub's removal. NOTUS reported in March 2026 that 195 enforcement matters were pending and later calculated that the agency had lacked a quorum for nearly 80% of Trump's second term. These figures describe the scale and duration of the enforcement backlog; they do not establish the merits of every pending case. It does not imply that the backlog resulted solely from one removal or that all pending matters involved the president.

title: MAGA Faction Ousts Kevin McCarthy as House Speaker
description_short: MAGA Faction Ousts Kevin McCarthy as House Speaker
description_medium: On October 3, 2023, Kevin McCarthy became the first Speaker in U.S. history to be removed by a motion to vacate, losing 216-210. The ouster was led by Rep. Matt Gaetz and aligned with Trump MAGA hardliners who believed McCarthy had made too many compromises. The vote threw the House into weeks of chaos as Republicans struggled to find a replacement. The dysfunction demonstrated that Trump MAGA faction could paralyze the Republican legislative agenda in pursuit of ideological purity.
description_long: The House removed Speaker Kevin McCarthy on October 3, 2023 by a 216–210 vote on a motion to vacate. McCarthy was the first House speaker removed through that mechanism. The vote created an immediate leadership vacancy and left Republicans struggling for weeks to select a replacement. These are concrete institutional consequences of the ouster, distinct from broader arguments about the motives of every member who voted for it. title: Trump Berates Zelensky in Oval Office Ambush on Live Television
description_short: Trump Berates Zelensky in Oval Office Ambush on Live Television
description_medium: During a televised Oval Office meeting on February 28, 2025, Trump and Vice President JD Vance sharply criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky over negotiations and continued U.S. support. The confrontation disrupted a planned minerals agreement and left Zelensky without the expected signing. The exchange strained the public relationship between Washington and Kyiv.
description_long: During a televised Oval Office meeting on February 28, 2025, Trump and Vice President JD Vance sharply challenged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky over negotiations and Ukraine's reliance on American support. Trump questioned Zelensky's leverage and warned that Ukraine could not continue the war without U.S. backing. The public confrontation disrupted a planned agreement concerning mineral resources, and Zelensky left without signing it. The meeting unsettled European leaders and raised questions about Washington's willingness to sustain support for Kyiv as Russia's invasion continued. The encounter marked a striking change in tone: a private diplomatic discussion became a widely broadcast dispute between the U.S. president and the leader of a country at war. The meeting did not itself end American assistance, but it made the terms and reliability of U.S. support a central issue for Ukraine and its allies, unsettling European partners.

description_short: Trump Pressures Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Arizona Officials to Overturn Results

The effort as a campaign directed at elected officials in swing states. The linked Politico report documents the pressure tactics and the dispute over certification.
description_long: After the 2020 election, Donald Trump and allies pressured officials in Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Arizona to reject, delay, or reverse certified results. The pressure formed part of a wider effort to challenge the outcome after votes had been counted. In Michigan, Republican state legislators faced demands connected to the certification process; similar efforts targeted officials in other closely contested states. The entry concerns attempts to influence public officials and the administration of an election, not a lawful recount that independently establishes fraud. The effort targeted state officials responsible for election administration, although their responses varied. The episode is important because certification is a central safeguard in the transfer of power, and attempts to overturn certified results can weaken confidence in elections even when they do not succeed.

title: Trump Ends Protections for Transgender Military Service Members
description_short: Trump Ends Protections for Transgender Military Service Members
description_medium: Trump announced in July 2017 that transgender people would be barred from military service, reversing the policy allowing open service. The announcement caught Pentagon leaders off guard, and the Joint Chiefs said the existing policy would remain pending formal direction. Federal courts later blocked implementation while challenges proceeded.
description_long: In July 2017, Trump announced that transgender people would no longer be permitted to serve in the U.S. military, reversing the policy that had allowed open service. The announcement surprised Pentagon leaders; the chairman of the Joint Chiefs said the current policy would remain in place until formal orders arrived. Trump cited medical costs and disruption, while studies at the time challenged the scale of those costs. The proposed restriction affected thousands of service members and raised questions about equal treatment, readiness, and the president's authority to change military policy. Federal courts issued injunctions that blocked implementation as legal challenges proceeded. The controversy therefore extended beyond the initial announcement: litigation and later policy decisions shaped whether the restriction could take effect. The episode became a major dispute over the rights of transgender service members and the process for adopting military policy.

title: 1.4 Million Lawfully Present Immigrants Lose Medicaid and Medicare Coverage
description_short: 1.4 Million Lawfully Present Immigrants Lose Medicaid and Medicare Coverage
description_medium: P.L. 119-21 restricted Medicaid and CHIP eligibility — effective October 1, 2026 — to lawful permanent residents, eliminating coverage for refugees, asylees, trafficking survivors, TPS holders, and parolees. CBO estimates 1.4 million lawfully present immigrants will become uninsured as a result, reducing federal spending by $131 billion by 2034. A separate provision eliminates ACA marketplace subsidies for lawfully present immigrants below the poverty line as of January 2026. Refugees and asylees without green cards will also be disenrolled from Medicare by January 4, 2027.
description_long: Immigration-status restrictions in P.L. 119-21 affecting Medicaid, CHIP, ACA subsidies and Medicare. It says Medicaid and CHIP changes take effect October 1, 2026 and would eliminate coverage for several groups of lawfully present immigrants, including refugees, asylees, trafficking survivors, TPS holders and parolees. CBO estimated that 1.4 million lawfully present immigrants would become uninsured, with a $131 billion reduction in federal spending by 2034. A separate provision ends Marketplace subsidies for lawfully present immigrants below the poverty line beginning January 2026, while refugees and asylees without green cards face Medicare disenrollment by January 4, 2027. These are different programs and implementation dates, rather than a single immediate termination for every immigrant. title: EEOC Moves to Drop Gender-Identity Discrimination Cases After Trump Orders
description_short: EEOC Moves to Drop Gender-Identity Discrimination Cases After Trump Orders

Clayton County holding (Title VII protects sexual orientation and gender identity) remained binding law.
